q: What is the derivative of ln x?
why: d/dx ln x = 1/x. This is why logs turn into percentage changes.
This isn't the power rule, because the x is in the exponent. eᵘ → eᵘ · u', so the answer is 2e^(2x).

q: Price elasticity of demand is −2. What does that mean?
o: A 1% price rise cuts quantity by about 2%
why: Elasticity compares percentage changes, not units, and |−2| > 1 means demand is elastic.

q: A straight-line demand curve has the same elasticity everywhere.
why: Myth. Elasticity is slope × P/Q, and P/Q changes along the line. Demand is elastic at high prices and inelastic at low ones.

q: ln x is defined at x = 0.
why: Myth. No power of e equals 0, so ln 0 doesn't exist.
